title: Tetrabiblos
author: Ptolemy (Ashmand trans)
description: Tetrabiblos (Quadripartitum, 'Four Books') by Claudius Ptolemy of Alexandria (second century CE), in the English translation by J. M. Ashmand (1822), with an appendix of related material from the Almagest on the aspects of the fixed stars. The most authoritative astrological text of the ancient and medieval world, it presents astrology as a natural science of celestial influence complementary to Ptolemy's astronomy. Book I defends astrology's possibility and sets out the powers of the planets, the signs, triplicities, houses, terms and aspects. Book II covers mundane astrology: the influence of the heavens on countries and peoples, eclipses and weather. Books III and IV treat the nativity: parents, siblings, sex, length of life, bodily form, temperament and disease, the quality of the soul, wealth, honour, marriage, children, travel and manner of death. It shaped Arabic, medieval and Renaissance astrology and remains a foundation of traditional practice.
